Zimbabwe bowled with much greater discipline and control this morning, with Blessing Muzarabani looking the most threatening of the lot and deservedly finishing with three wickets. JUST IN - One of Sri Lanka’s most enduring stalwarts, Angelo Mathews, has announced his retirement from Test cricket. The veteran all-rounder will bow out of the longest format following the first Test of the two-match series against Bangladesh in Galle next month. Mathews has, however, confirmed his availability for selection in white-ball cricket.

The gap in experience was glaring on the opening day, with none of the Zimbabwean players having previously played a Test in England. They lacked discipline and were unable to build any sustained pressure. To make matters worse, Richard Ngarava walked off during the second session with a back issue and didn’t bowl again for the rest of the day. Zimbabwe will be hoping he recovers in time to make an impact with the second new ball, which is just eight overs old. Can the visitors show some fight? Stay tuned to find out!

Centuries from Zak Crawley, Ben Duckett, and Ollie Pope powered England to a commanding 498 by stumps, with the Zimbabwean bowlers struggling to make any real impact. With this being a four-day Test, the focus now shifts to the home side's game management. How long will they bat before declaring? They will need to leave themselves enough time to bowl Zimbabwe out twice, so expect some intent early on.

Hello and welcome to Day 2 of the one-off Test between England and Zimbabwe at Trent Bridge in Nottingham. The opening day was one of dominance for the hosts as they surged well ahead in the contest after being put in to bat. Zimbabwe’s first day of Test cricket in England in 22 years could hardly have gone any worse.
... DAY 2, SESSION 1 ...

Right then, England take the opening day honours and will look to build on their advantage on Day 2. For Zimbabwe, their first Test in England after a 22-year hiatus has gotten off to the worst possible start. They will need to show the stomach for a fight when they return and respond strongly. The first ball on Day 2 will be bowled at 10 am GMT, but you can join us early for the build-up. Until then, take care and goodbye!

The pair kept the scoreboard ticking, and Zimbabwe’s woes deepened when Richard Ngarava walked off with a back issue shortly after Lunch. On a beautiful batting deck, Duckett, Crawley, and Ollie Pope made hay while the sun shone, with each going on to score a century. The second new ball proved a double-edged sword for the tourists. While it brought the wicket of Joe Root, it also leaked 45 runs in just 8 overs, with England ending the day just shy of 500.

A day of English dominance at Trent Bridge! It wasn’t entirely unexpected, especially after a wicketless first session that set the tone. From there, Zimbabwe were left playing catch-up on a deck that offered little assistance and they didn’t help their cause with inconsistent lines and lengths. Earlier in the day, Craig Ervine chose to bowl under overcast skies, but his pace quartet lacked the control to trouble the English openers. Ben Duckett and Zak Crawley started cautiously before getting into the groove to dispatch anything loose.

Meanwhile, for England, Ben Duckett completed his 100 in that session and was motoring along nicely before getting out against the run of play. Zak Crawley has ended the session in the 90s, so the Tea won’t taste that sweet for him as nervous 90s might play around his mind. Ollie Pope has looked at his fluent best as he is closing in on a half century. Zimbabwe are in dire need of wickets and they would be hoping for a bowler to put his hand up and take up the responsibility, else the next session could well be another run fest. So, do join us for the post-tea session shortly.

SESSION SUMMARY - 27 overs, 165 runs and 1 wicket. Tea Time here in Trent Bridge and England batters continue to dominate. The only positive for Zimbabwe in that session was that they got their first wicket as Wessly Madhevere struck in his very first over. There hasn’t been any real help from the wicket and Zimbabwean bowlers haven’t helped themselves one bit as they have continued to be wayward with their lengths. Richard Ngarava going off the field shortly after Lunch only made matters worse for them. Madhevere did find some turn and if that is any sign to go by, then we can expect Day 2 and Day 3 to be more helpful for the spinners.

Uppish but Zak Crawley gets away with it! On a length, outside off, Crawley flays at the delivery well away from his body. Gets an outside edge that goes aerially but through the vacant backward point region. Ben Curran runs around in the deep to his left and cuts it off. Two runs taken. That will be TEA on Day 11

For Zimbabwe, Blessing Muzarabani has looked threatening at times. Tanaka Chivanga has looked a touch raw but has got some swing, as he went past the edge of batters on multiple occasions. Zimbabwe need to get their act together as soon as possible, else this will be a long day for them. Do join us for the post-lunch session in a bit.

At Lunch on Day 1, England are well-placed with the score reading 130/0. Zimbabwean pacers haven’t hit the right areas consistently, and as a result, they have really failed to create consistent pressure on the English openers. All pacers have either been a tad short or full and have failed to hammer the good length area on a consistent basis. Both Ben Duckett and Zak Crawley have been in cruise control mode, having crossed their fifties and they would be looking to go big in the post-lunch session. Commentary.Commentary: DRINKS BREAK! A steady start for England, and they will be fairly pleased with how the first hour has unfolded. While there hasn’t been anything extravagant, there has been just enough movement in the air and off the pitch to keep the bowlers interested. That said, Zimbabwe haven’t challenged the English openers enough on the front foot. Interestingly, as Stuart Broad has noted, the impact of the heavy roller usually starts to fade after the first hour. That’s also when the lacquer begins to wear off the ball, potentially generating more movement. On a pitch that looks good for batting, the tourists need to make the most of this window.

Their pace attack, led by the seasoned Richard Ngarava, with Blessing Muzarabani sharing the new ball duties to create trouble right from the start. Which also means there will be a slight tweak in the rules, for instance, we can have a maximum of 98 overs bowled each day instead of 90, and there will be six and a half hours of play daily, whereas a five-day match typically has six hours of play, barring the extra time.
